claim: For every finite set D of distinct integers d >= 3 with gcd(D) = 1 and sum_{d in D} 1/(d-1) >= 1, and every integer k >= 1, there exists N(D,k) such that every integer n >= N(D,k) is a sum of finitely many labelled occurrences d^j with d in D and j >= k, each pair (d,j) used at most once; equal numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.

quadruple.statement: For every finite set D of distinct integers d >= 3 with gcd(D) = 1 and sum_{d in D} 1/(d-1) >= 1, and every integer k >= 1, there exists N(D,k) such that every integer n >= N(D,k) is a sum of finitely many labelled occurrences d^j with d in D and j >= k, each pair (d,j) used at most once; equal numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.
quadruple.stage: Finite labelled base-digit assignments in the ordered additive monoid of nonnegative integers, with the original integer power streams retained.

shape.objects: Every finite distinct base set D and its infinite locally finite labelled power stream; finite digit assignments are subsets of pairs (d,j). Disjoint assignments can be united and an included block can be replaced by a disjoint equal-sum block. Core Nat, Finset, integer sums and gcd formalize these objects. Finite assignments may be random variables but have no spread hypothesis and no continuous deformation parameter.
shape.quantifiers: Universal over every finite admissible D and every positive k, then there exists N, then universal over all n>=N, then existential over a finite legal assignment. The family and target integers are unbounded, but no uncountable object or set of reals is quantified.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no eventual coverage property, equivalently an input-dependent finite threshold N(D,k). An unspecified threshold settles the claim; no optimum numerical constant or upper density is requested.
shape.ambient_structure: Ordered integer addition coexists with exact heterogeneous base recursions and labelled support. The ambient supplies disjoint union and block replacement, but no common dilation closing all streams, no supplied structured-piece/bias system, no established pairwise-overlap parameter or spread condition for a useful probabilistic estimate, and no proved transport to another category.
shape.symmetries: Permutation of D and complementation in a fixed finite prefix preserve the corresponding exact sum relations. Adding a translated or dilated assignment is not a legal symmetry without a separate labelled support check. No closed family of structured random pieces is recorded.
shape.configuration: A finite positive sum using each allowed label once and no forbidden low exponent. Restricting or truncating a zero-cutoff representation may destroy it. An exchange must preserve its integer sum and the 0/1 labelled-coordinate constraint; signed identities alone do not meet the target.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal candidate: this is an existence and coverage problem, not optimization against a known counterconstruction.
shape.finite_certificates: A given finite assignment, finite switch or represented finite interval is exactly checkable, and a finite switch seed can be searched in increasing support size starting at one label if its domain is separately admitted. This does not give a finite certificate deciding the entire arbitrary-input infinite assertion, nor a proved finite residue. Small fixed subset-sum instances are computable, but no computation is admitted.
shape.monotonicity: Adding base labels or decreasing the cutoff preserves any proved representation. The smallest positive cutoff is k=1, whose arbitrary-D assertion remains open; the zero-cutoff neighbour is solved. No transfer bound uniform in growing k has been established.
shape.uniformity_parameter: All admissible finite D, with no bound on cardinality or largest base, every positive k, and every n beyond an input-dependent threshold. Reciprocal equality must remain included.
shape.proof_shape: Move 1 proves the legal disjoint-switch amplification and exact residual gap ledger in moves/01-support-ledger.md. A switch family with positive gaps h_1=1 and h_t<=1+sum_{u<t}h_u, baseline B and total reserved weight W=2B+H yields all integers >=B if S_{i-1}-a_i+(W-W_{i-1})>=2B-1 at every retained index. The all-input switch family is not constructed. The canonical root statement has all quantifiers explicit, but no complete proof or finite residue is available.
shape.neighbours: Known true: the zero-cutoff digit assertion via Brown's criterion; disjoint equal-step switch amplification for the BEGL96 positive-density infinite base supply; modular subset-sum coverage from collective gcd one; accepted all-future surplus. Open: the full fixed-D positive-cutoff assertion and its finite-deletion and central-seed relatives. Known false: the abstract strong-surplus-and-arithmetic-profile inference, accepted checkpoint-000010. These do not provide a property-reflecting category correspondence or a simpler ambient in which this exact positive-cutoff statement reads unchanged.
shape.known_bounds: BEGL96 proves the named cutoff-one examples and cutoff-dependent finite subsets of an infinite positive-density base supply, not all fixed D and all k. Accepted checkpoint-000009 gives all-future surplus but not a seed. The old early-seed, generic profile and Gaussian image have recorded failures; no complete direct invariant bound, useful per-target first moment, additional compression of the pure-power counterexample space, full finite residue, or constant independent of the cutoff is known. There is no proved equivalence between the proposed exchange mechanism and the root.
shape.missing_input: A legal variable-length switch family satisfying both the Brown gap inequalities and the exact residual-stream support ledger for every D,k. The inequalities are sufficient, not known equivalent to the root; the pure-power construction and its cost remain unproved.
shape.base_theory: Classical arithmetic and finite combinatorics within ZFC, covered by Lean's standard classical axioms. No uncountable threshold, guessing principle, extra axiom, independence claim, or hypothesis beyond this base theory is involved. Exact finite checks would remain within it, but any machine execution requires separate controlled admission.

known: BEGL96, Complete sequences of sets of integer powers, DOI 10.4064/aa-77-2-133-138: conjecture on p.133, disjoint finite-difference switches in Claims 2-3, modular coverage in Claim 4, limited families and examples on p.137.
Bergelson-Simmons, arXiv:1507.02208v2, DOI 10.4064/aa8221-10-2016: Examples 1.7-1.9 and Main Theorem 2.1 distinguish syndetic subset sums from completeness and require disjoint supplies.
Canonical sources/124.lean, Erdos124.erdos124.ne_zero: all k!=0, all finite distinct D, collective gcd one, reciprocal mass at least one; zero cutoff is a separate solved statement.

Accepted checkpoint-000009 / acceptance-000002: all-future prefix surplus tends to infinity for every admissible D,k and finite deletion, with labels retained. This does not supply a represented seed.
Accepted checkpoint-000010 / acceptance-000003 refutes only the abstract strong-surplus profile inference, not pure-power completeness.

Checkpoint-000011 and its independent local check exclude an ordinary Gaussian approximation for fixed finite pure-power prefix laws; they establish no root theorem and do not exclude non-Gaussian methods.
